proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Complete randomization fixes both potential-outcome lists and the arm count. The iid encouragement model instead samples independent whole-unit potential vectors and independent encouragements. Known-Gaussian planning stipulates independent Gaussian arm observations with known variances. The manuscript consistently separates their targets and uncertainty; no finite-population normal limit is inferred from a variance formula.

proof_audit.claim: Inclusion moments and exact finite variance
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Counting single and pair inclusions gives p and n1(n1-1)/(N(N-1)), with the pair count zero at n1=1. Negative off-diagonal covariance follows from the fixed count. Writing the random part as a linear combination of indicators yields the centered coefficient sum and then S1 squared/n1 plus S0 squared/n0 minus S_tau squared/N. No constant-effect assumption enters this identity. Independent Bernoulli assignment changes both joint moments and arm-count denominators.

proof_audit.claim: Sample variance and a finite weak-average interval
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: The pair-distance identity with denominator m(m-1) and pair inclusion probability proves unbiased sample arm variances when m is at least two. Hence Neyman conservatism is in expectation, with the supplied realized counterexample below the true variance. The bounded-product variance inequality, the N/(N-1) conversion and Chebyshev prove the known-range weak-average coverage statement. Its closed interval is conservative at the possible equality boundary; zero range gives exactness. Observed extrema and Gaussian critical values are correctly excluded.

proof_audit.claim: Weighted ranks, ties, sharp imputation and inversion
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Grouping equal statistic levels and accumulating their positive assignment masses proves the inclusive rank inequality for nonuniform laws. The strict-tail example is invalid precisely because it omits the tied observed level. Subtracting c times actual assignment imputes the untreated list only under a sharp constant effect. Ordering, endpoint ties and improving exchanges prove acceptance [3,7] on the whole real line. The independent subset-polynomial certificate derives every comparison root and checks all point and open cells, including both unbounded tails. Repeated-assignment coverage is not truth for every realized set or heterogeneous-average coverage.

The true effect generates each observed table before applying the unchanged sharp-zero procedure. The exact rejection counts are therefore alternative probabilities, not null p-values relabeled as power. A balanced allocation and its distinct complement always have opposite contrasts and equal absolute statistics, so the minimum inclusive probability is 2/20. The small-design nonmonotone power is correctly restricted to this specified discrete procedure.

Independent stratum draws make cross-stratum covariance zero; the full-population estimator uses population shares and squared shares in its variance. Unequal treatment fractions change the naive pooled baseline mixture. Singleton cells lack ordinary sample variances even when a full synthetic potential table supplies oracle design variance. Cluster means target an average across clusters; unequal cluster size generally changes the relationship to an average across people.

proof_audit.claim: Known-Gaussian power, integer allocation and cluster information
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: The exact Gaussian contrast yields both rejection tails. Its power is increasing in positive absolute noncentrality. Strict convexity and endpoint divergence give the unique continuous allocation; monotonicity on each side restricts integer candidates to adjacent integers. Adding one observation to an existing optimum strictly lowers attainable variance, so the two sample-size boundary checks establish global minima. The independent Gaussian common/idiosyncratic decomposition gives the cluster variance and fixed-cluster information floor; the standard-error factor is the square root of the variance factor. Assignment independence and known variances are stated.

proof_audit.claim: Assignment ITT, LATE and treated-population mixtures
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Random encouragement identifies assignment potential-outcome differences before exclusion. Binary consistency, independence, exclusion, monotonicity and positive complier mass then yield the complier decomposition inherited from accepted c03 and rederived here. The ATE and actual-treated effect use different type weights. Specifying encouragement probability is essential for the latter mixture. The direct assignment increment preserves the ITT interpretation but breaks treatment-only exclusion.

The arm-mean identity has a random empirical denominator. LLN and the joint finite-second-moment iid CLT give signed arm influences; the exact ratio identity retains the outcome/treatment covariance. Positive arm probabilities and fixed nonzero population first stage make undefined finite events asymptotically negligible but do not remove them in actual data. Fitted influence coefficients converge on events with denominators bounded away from zero; an envelope proportional to 1+|Y|, the LLN for 1+Y squared and Cauchy-Schwarz establish feasible covariance consistency. Positive limiting variance is separately needed for studentization. No uniform weak-first-stage inference is claimed.

proof_audit.claim: Exposure mapping, HT means and full covariance
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Correct mapping makes the observed outcome equal the specified exposure outcome on its indicator event, so positive marginal probability proves HT unbiasedness. Expanding all pairs of indicators proves the full covariance identity, including repeated units and mutually exclusive exposures. Positive marginals do not imply joint support. The entire synthetic potential table allows an oracle covariance calculation, while an experiment need not reveal every product. Fixed-one assignment loses center untreated-unexposed support; the remote-effect witness independently breaks the old exposure map.

proof_audit.claim: Bounded attrition and complete observed-law sharpness
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Total expectation bounds each missing arm mean without MAR. Opposite endpoint completions preserve the distribution of (Z,R,Y when observed), not just its first moments, and independent mixtures attain every intermediate effect. The independent-response construction is sufficient, not necessary: the peer also verifies both extreme feasible response couplings with identical observed law and endpoint effects. Equal response rates neither establish equal identities nor rule out outcome selection. A population identified interval remains distinct from its sample-estimated uncertainty.

proof_audit.claim: Instruction, exact questions and research critique
proof_audit.independent_reasoning: Every proof method requested by the twelve prompts is taught or within a specifically accepted prerequisite. The referee rubric covers all eight named issues and requires actual evidence or repair proposals; it does not grade a predetermined sign or policy conclusion. Teach-back and all four retention answers are coherent with the targets and probability laws proved earlier.

prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Subset counts give EZ_i=n1/N and EZ_iZ_j=n1(n1-1)/(N(N-1)). The centered coefficient expansion proves unbiasedness and S1 squared/n1+S0 squared/n0-S_tau squared/N. Bernoulli pair covariance is zero, with random and possibly empty arm counts; fixed-count denominators cannot be reused unchanged.

The pair-distance sample variance has denominator m(m-1); pair inclusion proves its unbiasedness for m>=2. In the 0,2,4 assignment the mean contrast is -1 and estimated variance 8/3, below 44/15. The full-population bounds imply C=37/5 and 90% halfwidth sqrt(74)=8.602325 rounded. The proof uses prospective counterfactual ranges and Chebyshev, not observed extrema or a normal pivot.

For probabilities (1/2,1/4,1/4) and statistics (2,2,0), inclusive values are (3/4,3/4,1) and rejection mass is zero at 1/4. Strict tails give (0,0,3/4) and invalid rejection mass 3/4. Grouped cumulative masses prove the general rank result. A weak average-zero null does not impute unit-specific missing outcomes.

The observed contrast is 5-c after adjustment. Outside [3,7], only the observed extreme allocation and its complement are as extreme, giving p=1/10 and rejection. At 3 and 7 tied swaps produce p=1/5; at 5 the statistic is zero and p=1. Interior swaps increase extremeness, so the entire interval is accepted. Exact zero-null rejection counts across actual assignments are 2,1,2,4,8 for effects 0 through 4. No p<=1/20 is possible. Excluding a true value in one tail realization does not refute repeated-assignment coverage.

The population stratum weights remain 1/2 each. Independent 1-of-4 and 3-of-4 assignment yields 16 choices, target 2 and variance 10/9. Expected pooled arm means are 11 and 4, producing 7 instead of 2. Single treated/control cells do not support sample variance estimation. Full potential-table variance information is distinct from observable sample information.

Both normal tails give Phi(lambda-z)+Phi(-lambda-z). Strict convexity yields p=3/4 for variances 9 and 1; compare adjacent integer allocations. Exhaustive independent finite optimization confirms 94/31 at N=125, variance 373/2914 and power .798168, versus 94/32 at N=126, variance 191/1504 and power .801270. Equal arms give powers .797546 at total 156 and .802541 at 158. Strict improvement of attainable variance with N proves minima 126 and 158. Changed variances/reference law, effect or size/power target, costs/allocation constraints, clustering or attrition require a new calculation.

A cluster mean has variance sigma_A squared+sigma_e squared/m; J independent clusters per arm give twice this divided by J. With J=m=10 and components 1 and 4, the variance is 7/25 versus the independent-row 1/10. Their ratio is 14/5 and the standard-error factor is sqrt(14/5)=1.673320 rounded. Zero common variance gives factor one; fixed J with growing m retains variance 2 sigma_A squared/J, here 1/5. Unequal cluster sizes require a separate target/weight choice.

The random-arm quotient and joint CLT give signed influences and (psi_Y-beta psi_D)/gamma, including their covariance. Nonempty arms, a nonzero fitted first stage and a positive limiting variance remain separate qualifications. Q=Y-2D takes values 1,4,3 with mean 17/8 and variance 87/64; its contrast variance and division by (3/8) squared yield 116/3. A direct Z/2 increment makes ITT 5/4 and the ratio 10/3, with unchanged uptake and treatment effect 2 at fixed encouragement. Exclusion fails while assignment identification survives.

Exposure-indicator expectations prove the HT mean; expanding every indicator product gives the full joint covariance. The eight contrast outcomes are (-32/3,32/3,16,0,0,16,0,0), with mean 4, second moment 832/9 and variance 688/9. Adjacent treated-unexposed events have zero joint probability. A full synthetic table permits oracle product evaluation, whereas a single experiment does not generally observe all such potential products.

Endpoints have probabilities (1-p) squared and p(1-p) for 00 and 10; the center has (1-p) cubed and p(1-p) squared. Under fixed-one assignment the center 00 event is impossible. Changing that unrestricted potential outcome leaves the design observed law unchanged. Separately, assignments 000 and 001 give unit 0 the same old 00 label but augmented outcomes 1 and 3. Inclusion weights cannot repair a misspecified mapping.

The arm mean r_d m_d+(1-r_d)u_d and bounded u_d give the lower and upper effect endpoints. Independent potential-response cells of masses 16/25,4/25,4/25,1/25 support both full-law completions: lower means 32/5 and 34/5, upper means 42/5 and 24/5, yielding effects -2/5 and 18/5. Their complete observed distributions agree. An assignment-independent mixture keeps that distribution and interpolates all effects. Equal response rates and precise respondent means do not supply missing counterfactual outcomes.

The solution and open rubric require the actual branch design law, assignment unit and target; distinguish randomized encouragement ITT from selected receipt regression and qualified LATE; investigate recommendation spillovers and exposure support; request follow-up identities and outcome bounds; disclose selection among twelve outcomes; and separate prospective model-based power from observed uncertainty with estimated variances. Each unresolved claim needs a specific evidence request or valid repair. No generic permutation, multiplicity correction or policy conclusion is asserted without its own justification.

teaching_audit.teach_back: The criteria require a design-to-target-to-uncertainty argument using a finite inclusion identity, compliance distinction and one actual interference or attrition counterexample. They correctly reject automatic ATE/normal/transport conclusions.
retention: Expected Neyman excess remains valid when a particular estimate is below true variance.
The inclusive balanced complement-symmetric p-value is at least 2/20, never .05.
Growing rows within the same ten independent clusters per arm leaves variance 1/5.
Measuring treatment nonrespondents at outcome 4 fixes that mean at 36/5 and narrows the ATE interval to [2/5,12/5].

independent_numerical_method.finite_assignments: Enumerate named treatment subsets using exact fractions; compute each observed arm variance from pair distances. Verify the complete assignment distribution, the coefficient-order-statistic support, single/pair inclusion probabilities including one treated unit, the treatment-heterogeneity correction and constant-effect/zero-range boundaries.
independent_numerical_method.fisher: A dynamic-programming subset-generating polynomial records selected count, overlap with the observed treated subset and outcome sum. Its coefficients reconstruct null tails. Squared-tail comparisons factor into affine terms with exact roots 3,4,9/2,5,11/2,6,7. The seven roots and eight open cells exhaust the real line, including both unbounded components; signs cannot change away from these roots. Alternative tables are generated independently for all twenty actual assignments at five true effects.
independent_numerical_method.strata: Convolve the two independent stratum contrast laws and reconstruct pooled observed means. Compare population weights with unequal treatment shares, rather than assuming the pooled target is unchanged.
independent_numerical_method.gaussian: Integrate the exponential Taylor series in 50-digit Decimal arithmetic and invert the CDF by bisection. The code does not use author erfc/NormalDist calculations. On |x|<=8, terms decrease beyond index 32; the alternating remainder at cutoff is below 1e-43 before float conversion, with sufficient precision for cancellation. Displays are checked to absolute 5e-7 and internal Gaussian symmetries to 2e-12. Exhaustive integer optimization is restricted to the two substantive boundary totals. Monotone optimal variance supplies the proof across all smaller totals.
independent_numerical_method.clusters: Reconstruct independent common-shock and idiosyncratic-shock coefficients in the final contrast. The sum of coefficient squares times component variances directly yields the information retained by fixed clusters.
independent_numerical_method.encouragement: Form the six-atom observed law and differentiate the complete rational mean-difference ratio along each observed-probability perturbation. Compare the resulting joint covariance with an independent residual-type calculation. A sixteen-row sample independently reconstructs feasible covariance, and direct assignment effects/changed assignment probability check interpretation and composition.
independent_numerical_method.interference: Represent the six target exposure indicators as a random vector over the eight assignments. Calculate its entire 6-by-6 covariance matrix and quadratic-form contrast variance, under p=1/2 and p=1/3. Mapping and marginal support failures are explicitly exercised, with positive marginal and zero joint probabilities distinguished.
independent_numerical_method.attrition: Use complete potential-response laws with joint response probability 3/5,16/25,4/5, covering the two extreme couplings and the author independent construction. Every endpoint has exactly the same observed (Z,R,Y when observed) distribution. A 3/4-1/4 endpoint mixture demonstrates an interior value; the analytic mixture argument covers all interior values. Complete response, zero response and actual extra follow-up test the identification boundaries.
independent_numerical_method.visible_values: All 84 exact numerical markers and six six-decimal markers are independently reconstructed. All twelve exact IDs are paired with solutions. Unmarked formulas, table inputs and proof statements were read analytically.
independent_numerical_method.domain: Read-only check() has no external input file or output option. Private finite routines have explicit declared bounds: at most ten assignment units, 512 allocation observations, 32 observed atoms, exact scalar magnitude at most one million and Gaussian numerical arguments within eight standard deviations. Actual exception tests, including strict JSON failures, remain active under -O.
independent_numerical_method.limits: Finite numerical execution is not a proof of an asymptotic theorem or substantive experiment assumptions. The analytic audit above supplies the separate proof review.

peer_summary.gaussian_method: 50-digit exponential-series integration and bisection; bounded absolute argument 8
intervention_scopes: Singleton inclusion boundary, changed fixed counts and constant effects separate finite covariance and variance-estimation scope.
Subset-generating polynomials certify every real Fisher candidate; alternative generation and unequal tied masses check the actual rejection law.
Changing treatment fractions inside fixed strata preserves the weighted estimand while moving the naive pooled expectation.
Decimal exponential integration and quantile bisection verify Gaussian powers; full integer optimization and independent latent-shock coefficients certify allocation and cluster information.
Observed-law quotient derivatives and actual sample frequencies check covariance-aware Wald inference; direct encouragement and assignment frequency separate ITT, LATE, ATT and precision.
Six exposure indicators reconstruct the full covariance; nonuniform assignment and absent joint or marginal support distinguish mean, variance and mapping identification.
Extreme, independent and common potential-response couplings give the same complete observed law and sharp bounds; mixtures and measured follow-up separate identification from sampling precision.
